title: Find Time Required to Eliminate Bacterial Strains
summary: Given an integer array timeReq and an integer splitTime, determine the minimum time required to eliminate all bacterial strains.
statement: Given an integer array timeReq and an integer splitTime, determine the minimum time required to eliminate all bacterial strains. Each bacterial strain takes timeReq[i] units of time to be eliminated. A single white blood cell (WBC) can eliminate one bacterial strain, after which it can split into two WBCs after splitTime units of time, with each working on a separate strain. Only one WBC can work on a single bacterial strain at a time.
constraints: time_req contains 2 to 100,000 positive task durations.
One worker may finish one strain and stop, or spend split_time to create two workers that proceed in parallel.
Strains may be assigned in any order; minimize the time when every strain is eliminated.
reference_solution:
def minimum_elimination_time(time_req, split_time):
    import heapq
    heap=list(time_req);heapq.heapify(heap)
    while len(heap)>1:
        first=heapq.heappop(heap);second=heapq.heappop(heap)
        heapq.heappush(heap,second+split_time)
    return heap[0]

hints: A split node finishes at split_time plus the slower child; building the schedule backward therefore combines the two smallest completion requirements.
Use a min-heap and repeatedly replace the two smallest requirements by the larger one plus split_time.
Heapify a copy, pop two values, push second+split_time, and continue to one value.
The standard exchange argument moves the two earliest leaves to deepest sibling positions without worsening the maximum completion time.

tests.explanation: Split once for the ten-unit strain and split the other branch again for four and five; all finish by time twelve.
One split lets both eliminations run in parallel, finishing after fifteen units.
